chunks: Some of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Yaḥyā ibn Musāwir, from Saʿd al-Iskāf, who said:

I came to Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) regarding some matter for which I used to come to him. He began saying, “Do not be hasty,” until the sun grew hot upon me and I began following the patches of shade. It was not long before a people came out toward me as though they were yellow locusts; they had woolen garments upon them, and worship had worn them down. He said: By Allah, the beauty of the people’s appearance made me forget what I had been occupied with.

Then when I entered upon him, he said to me, “I see that I have caused hardship for you.” I said, “Yes, by Allah. A people passed by me and made me forget what I had been occupied with. I have never seen a people with a more beautiful appearance than them, in the dress of one man, as though their colors were like yellow locusts; worship had worn them down.” So he said, “O Saʿd, did you see them?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “Those are your brothers from the jinn.” He said: So I said, “Do they come to you?” He said, “Yes, they come to us, asking us about the teachings of their religion, and their halal (permissible) and their haram (forbidden).”

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Muḥammad al-Bāqir (عليه السلام), the one being visited in the narration
key_terms.الْأَفْيَاءَ: patches of shade sought during the heat of the sun
key_terms.الْجَرَادُ الصُّفْرُ: yellow locusts, used as a simile for the group’s appearance
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: the jinn, identified by the Imam as the group Saʿd saw
key_terms.الْعِبَادَةُ: worship, whose intensity had visibly affected them
key_terms.حَرَامِهِمْ: that which is forbidden for them in religion
key_terms.حَلَالِهِمْ: that which is permissible for them in religion
key_terms.مَعَالِمِ دِينِهِمْ: the teachings and defining features of their religion

ai.seo_question: Do the jinn come to the Imams (عليهم السلام) to ask about their religion?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates Saʿd al-Iskāf’s encounter with a remarkable group whose appearance reflected intense worship, after which Imam Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) informs him that they were jinn. It highlights that the jinn also come to the Imam to seek guidance concerning the teachings of their religion and matters of halal (permissible) and haram (forbidden).

en.hubeali: Some of our companions, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Yahya Bin Musawir, from Sa’ad Al Iskaf who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding some of what I used to go to him<sup>asws</sup> for, so he<sup>asws</sup> went on to say: ‘Not now’, until the sun was very hot upon me, and I went to follow the shades. So, it was not long before there came out to me a group, as if they were locusts, there being paleness upon them, slim, the worship having affected them. So, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I had never been so awed by the beauty of the group.

So when I went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> see that I<sup>asws</sup> have been difficult upon you’. I said, ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! It had comforted me what I was in, by a group which passed by me. I have never seen a people more beautiful in awe than them in uniform like one man, as if their colours were like the locusts, the paleness due to the worship having had affected them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Sa’d! You saw them?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are your brethren from the Jinn’. So I said, ‘They come to you<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They do come to us<sup>asws</sup>, asking us<sup>asws</sup> about the information of their Religion, and their Permissible and their Prohibitions’.
en.sarwar: 1. Certain persons of our people have narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from Yahya ibn Musawir from Sa‘d al-Askaf who has said the following.

“On one of the occasion of my meeting with abu Ja‘far (a.s.) when I went tosee him he asked me to wait until the sun became very hot on me. I tried to follow the shadow from the sun. No very long thereafter a people came out of his presence that looked like locusts dressed in large gowns and very oale and slim due to extensive worshipping. Their beautiful scene made me to forget other things.

When I went in the presence of the Imam (a.s.) he said, “I am afraid I caused you hardships.” I said, “Yes, it was difficult but, by Allah, I forgot other things when I saw them. A people passed by the like of whose beauty I had not seen before. They looked like locusts and pale and slim due to worshipping a great deal.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “O Sa‘d , did you see them?” I said, “Yes, I saw them.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “They are your brethren from Jinns.” The narrator has said that he asked The Imam (a.s.), “Do they come to you?” He said, “Yes, they come to us for religious instructions and to learn the lawful and unlawful matters.”
